title: Unbounded coefficient forgetting identifies canonical etale exchange
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be any commutative ring and let $f:X\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $g:Y'\to Y$, $g':X'\to X$ form a cartesian square of schemes [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Use the unbounded derived categories $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ and $D(T_{\mathrm{et}})$ of [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. For each corner $T$ let $U_T:D(T_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)\to D(T_{\mathrm{et}})$ be termwise forgetting of the constant-ring module structure [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. This functor is exact and conservative (it reflects isomorphisms), with $\mathcal H^i(U_TK)=U_T\mathcal H^i(K)$. For every edge $u:A\to B$ there are canonical natural isomorphisms $a_u:U_Au^{-1}_{\Lambda}\xrightarrow{\sim}u^{-1}_{\mathbf Z}U_B$ and $b_u:U_BRu_{*,\Lambda}\xrightarrow{\sim}Ru_{*,\mathbf Z}U_A$. Here $a_u$ is the termwise inverse-image comparison on underlying abelian sheaves, and $b_u$ is the canonical comparison obtained by choosing a module K-injective representative $I$ and an abelian K-injective replacement $U_AI\to J$ [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions], then taking the class of $u_*U_AI\to u_*J$. No preservation of K-injectivity by $U_A$ is asserted.
For $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ define the endpoint isomorphisms by the typed composites
$$s_K:U_{Y'}g^{-1}_{\Lambda}Rf_{*,\Lambda}K\xrightarrow{a_g(Rf_{*,\Lambda}K)}g^{-1}_{\mathbf Z}U_YRf_{*,\Lambda}K\xrightarrow{g^{-1}_{\mathbf Z}b_f(K)}g^{-1}_{\mathbf Z}Rf_{*,\mathbf Z}U_XK,$$
$$t_K:U_{Y'}Rf'_{*,\Lambda}g'^{-1}_{\Lambda}K\xrightarrow{b_{f'}(g'^{-1}_{\Lambda}K)}Rf'_{*,\mathbf Z}U_{X'}g'^{-1}_{\Lambda}K\xrightarrow{Rf'_{*,\mathbf Z}a_{g'}(K)}Rf'_{*,\mathbf Z}g'^{-1}_{\mathbf Z}U_XK.$$
Thus $s_K$ and $t_K$ identify the forgotten source and target of the exchange with their abelian versions. For the canonical unbounded adjunction-mate exchange maps of [def-kun-unbounded-exchange], using the same definition at $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$ for abelian sheaves, one has
$$t_K\circ U_{Y'}(\operatorname{Ex}^{\Lambda}_{\square,K})=\operatorname{Ex}^{\mathbf Z}_{\square,U_XK}\circ s_K.$$
No properness, torsion, boundedness, finiteness of $\Lambda$, or isomorphism assertion for either exchange map is assumed or concluded.

proof.text: Forgetting a module action preserves kernels sectionwise and cokernels by sheafifying the same underlying additive quotient. The inverse of a bijective module homomorphism is module-linear: if y=h(x), then h^{-1}(ry)=rx. Thus the sheaf forgetful functor is exact and reflects isomorphisms. The exact-functor factorization induces its triangulated unbounded functor; the exact cohomology comparison gives H^i(UK)=U H^i(K). If U(h) is invertible, all U H^i(h) are invertible, hence all H^i(h) are invertible by the preceding sheaf argument; the derived cohomology criterion makes h invertible. This proves conservativity for arbitrary unbounded complexes.

source.place: Tag 0D6J, lemma-modules-abelian-unbounded; exact forgetting and cohomology criterion

proof.text: For an edge u, the module inverse image is the abelian inverse image with transported action, and its sheaf unit and counit are the underlying abelian ones. Hence forgetting gives the canonical inverse-image comparison and a compatible ordinary adjoint square, with direct-image comparison the sectionwise identity. Apply the localization universal property (2) to its termwise inverse-image isomorphism: this gives a_u. Applying the same property to the two composite inverse images gives, for theta:f'^{-1}g^{-1}->g'^{-1}f^{-1}, the equality theta_Z U(Rf K) o f'^{-1}_Z a_g(Rf K) o a_f'(g^{-1}_Lambda Rf K) = g'^{-1}_Z a_f(Rf K) o a_g'(f^{-1}_Lambda Rf K) o U(theta_Lambda,Rf K). Both sides are the same sheaf composition comparison degree by degree, and localization (3) preserves this equality.

View forgetting as the direct image of the identity-topos ring map Z_T->Lambda_T. Its derived direct image is termwise U by exactness. Factor the ringed-topos morphism (A,Lambda_A)->(B,Z_B) in the two ways, through (B,Lambda_B) and through (A,Z_A). The ringed-topos composition theorem identifies both composites with its total right derived image, giving b_u:U_B Ru_Lambda->Ru_Z U_A. In the first factorization no replacement after u_*I is needed, since the last functor is exact. In the second choose U_AI->J abelian K-injective; the normalized composition comparison is exactly the class of u_*U_AI->u_*J. The theorem therefore gives invertibility and naturality for the prescribed b_u, without assuming U_AI K-injective. It also shows U_B Ru_Lambda, with its comparison unit, is the right derived functor of U_B u_*Lambda.

Apply the general derived adjoint-square comparison to the ordinary compatible square of step 2 and the right-derived postcomposition property of step 3. It gives b_u(u^{-1}M) U_B(eta_Lambda,M)=Ru_Z(a_u(M))^{-1} eta_Z,U_B M and U_A(epsilon_Lambda,N)=epsilon_Z,U_A N o u^{-1}_Z(b_u(N)) o a_u(Ru_Lambda N). These identities are for the fixed resolution-normalized comparison b_u; they do not merely assert the existence of some compatible isomorphism.

proof.text:
Write $L=f^{-1}$, $L'=f'^{-1}$, $H=g^{-1}$, $H'=g'^{-1}$, $R=Rf_*$ and $R'=Rf'_*$. Subscripts $0$ denote abelian derived functors; $U$ has the corner dictated by its argument. Put $x=\operatorname{Ex}^{\Lambda}_{\square,K}$. The mate definition says $\varepsilon'_{\Lambda,H'K}L'(x)=H'(\varepsilon_{\Lambda,K})\theta_{\Lambda,RK}$. For $y=t_KU(x)$ its transpose is $\varepsilon'_{0,H'_0UK}L'_0(y)$. Naturality of $\varepsilon'_0$, the counit equation of step 4 for $f'$, and naturality of $a_{f'}$ give
$$y^\flat=a_{g'}(K)U(\varepsilon'_{\Lambda,H'K})U(L'(x))a_{f'}(HRK)^{-1}.$$
Substitute the mate equation and use naturality of $a_{g'}$ at $\varepsilon_{\Lambda,K}:LRK\to K$:
$$y^\flat=H'_0(U\varepsilon_{\Lambda,K})a_{g'}(LRK)U(\theta_{\Lambda,RK})a_{f'}(HRK)^{-1}.$$
The counit equation for $f$ is $U\varepsilon_{\Lambda,K}=\varepsilon_{0,UK}L_0(b_f(K))a_f(RK)$. The square equation of step 2, after cancelling $a_{f'}(HRK)$, is
$$H'_0(a_f(RK))a_{g'}(LRK)U(\theta_{\Lambda,RK})a_{f'}(HRK)^{-1}=\theta_{0,URK}L'_0(a_g(RK)).$$
Consequently
$$y^\flat=H'_0(\varepsilon_{0,UK})H'_0L_0(b_f(K))\theta_{0,URK}L'_0(a_g(RK))=H'_0(\varepsilon_{0,UK})\theta_{0,R_0UK}L'_0(H_0(b_f(K))a_g(RK)).$$
The last equality is naturality of $\theta_0$ at $b_f(K):URK\to R_0UK$. Since $s_K=H_0(b_f(K))a_g(RK)$, this is the transpose of $\operatorname{Ex}^{\mathbf Z}_{\square,UK}s_K$. Injectivity of the adjunction Hom bijection proves the required equality. Steps 2 and 3 make every component of $s,t$ a natural isomorphism.
